hints.title: In-Order Sequence Anomaly Obstacle
hints.text: In a valid search tree, an in-order traversal produces values in strictly increasing order. If exactly two nodes were swapped, how will the violations appear in the traversed sequence?

hints.title: Dual Inversion Detection Invariant
hints.text: The in-order sequence contains either one or two inversions where a previous value exceeds the current value. The swapped nodes correspond to the first anomalous value and the last.

hints.title: In-Order Pointers Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Traverse in-order while maintaining a pointer to the previous visited node. When prev.val > curr.val, mark first = prev if first is null, and always update second = curr. After completing traversal, swap first.val and second.val in place.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (2 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Single in-order traversal tracking pointers to two anomalous nodes followed by an O(1) value swap.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting node values requires an auxiliary array of size O(N) and two full traversals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly handling both adjacent swaps (single drop) and non-adjacent swaps (two drops).
